## 2. Cost per right answer and the tools-over-no-tools multiplier

Cost per right answer = tokens of the cell / right answers. Raw = input + output; price-weighted = input + 5 x output (a 5:1 output:input price, the ratio of both Claude list prices). Multiplier = tools arm / no-tools arm, same trials (below 1: the tool arm is cheaper per right answer). `gen_common.multiplier_boot`, the same draws for both arms.

## 4. Where the input of a tool trial goes

Share of the tool arm's input tokens that is (a) the first prompt (system message, tool list, task), sent again with every request; (b) the model's own earlier replies (mostly the tool calls, which copy the PDDL), re-read; (c) tool output, re-read. Claude: exact, from the per-request counts. Open models: (a) from the first-prompt offset (section 8), (b) and (c) split by characters, an estimate.

## 5. Output length, the output cap, the window, and tokens on wrong answers

Output tokens per trial (tool arm: summed over requests; Claude also the final reply alone). At cap: the final reply stopped at the output cap (open tool arms: not counting a final turn that ran out of window). Window full: the final request was refused or clipped because the prompt filled the 16,384-token window. Wrong share: share of the cell's tokens spent on trials that end wrong.

## 7. Window-full trials of the open tool arms

Trials whose final request was refused (no room) or clipped. A refused request is stored as 16,384 input tokens (vLLM's lower bound for the 1-token probe), although the server generated nothing and its real prompt was longer. For the two-request trials whose second request was refused: summed input minus the first prompt, median [min, max] (16,384 when the first-prompt offset is right). ## 9. A second metric: coverage at a token budget

Coverage at budget B = share of a cell's trials that are right AND used at most B tokens (input + output, summed over the requests). The budget is applied after the fact: no model was run under a budget, so the curve says how many trials would have finished right within B if nothing else changed. Over budget counts as not solved. Checked: at no limit it equals the filed right counts of 38 cells, and the paired difference equals the 22 filed contrasts (estimate and interval).

## 10. Tools against no tools under prompt caching

cost(c, p) = U + c x C + p x O (Yang et al., arXiv:2611.22238): U uncached input, C cached input, O output, c and p the prices of a cached and an output token relative to an uncached input token. No run had a caching discount: every figure before this section is c = 1. Scenario 1 (own hits): request t >= 2 of a trial reads the previous request's whole prompt from the cache; a no-tools trial is one request, C = 0. Everything here is computed, not billed.

**How C was obtained.** open, two requests (C = P_1, exact up to the offset): 20899; open, three or more requests (bounded): 2141; open, refused final request (C exact with it; bounded without it): 174; open, refused final request (C exact with it; exact without it): 868; open, one request (C = 0): 3278; Claude, two or more requests (exact): 8996; Claude, one request (C = 0): 124. Claude requests whose prompt was shorter than the previous one: 0. Open models with three or more requests: (n-1) P_1 <= C <= S (n-1)/n, point value by characters. A refused final request (stored as 16,384 input tokens that never ran) is kept in the main rows (then C = S - 16,384 exactly) and taken out in the rows so marked.

### 10.1 Multiplier, tokens per right answer, tools / no tools, by cache price

### 10.5 Scenario 2, labelled apart: the static prefix also cached across trials

The tool arm's extra static prefix (its system text and the seven tool descriptions, less the no-tools system text) = first-request input of the tool arm minus the input of the no-tools arm, same trial. In this scenario it is also read from the cache on the first request of every trial. This depends on traffic (requests within the cache lifetime, a minimum cacheable length), not on the trial. The no-tools arm's own system text, also static, is not credited (its size cannot be measured from the rows), so this scenario leans slightly toward the tools.
